intro: When you search for an interior architect near me, you are usually planning to change how the inside of your home or premises works — knocking rooms together, reworking a layout, or giving a tired space a proper redesign. You want someone local enough to visit, measure up and understand the building, and you want to know who you are actually hiring. We can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an interior architect usually need
need_lead: Most enquiries like yours come from people who have a space that no longer suits them and want professional help to reshape it properly.
needs: You want to reconfigure the inside of your home — moving walls, rethinking the kitchen or opening up the back of the house — and need someone who can turn that into workable drawings.
You are refurbishing a flat or period property and want the layout, finishes and lighting thought through together rather than piecemeal.
You run a shop, café, salon or office and need a fit-out designed so the space works for staff and customers alike.
You have a clear picture of how you want the space to feel but need someone to translate it into plans that a builder can actually price and follow.
You are unsure whether your plans touch structural walls or need building regulations approval, and want guidance from someone used to navigating those processes.
context: "Architect" is a protected title in the UK. Only people on the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register can call themselves architects, and they must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance. Many practices are also RIBA Chartered Practices. Architectural designers and technologists can do excellent work too, but they are not registered architects, so it is worth knowing which you are hiring — especially when the search brings up a mix of titles.

Interior work often looks simpler than it is. Structural changes need engineers, building regulations still apply, and lighting design transforms spaces, so a good professional will tell you early what else needs to be brought in. Before you appoint anyone, check the ARB register and ask for a written appointment that sets out services, fees and responsibilities.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Describe the property — its type, rough age and whether it is a house, flat or commercial premises — so we can match you with someone used to that kind of building.
Explain which rooms or areas you want to change and what you hope the finished space will do for you.
Say whether the work is a refurbishment, a fit-out or a redesign of the existing layout, as these call for different experience.
Mention whether you already know of any structural walls involved or whether planning permission or building regulations approval may be needed.
Note your rough budget range in your own words rather than a fixed figure, so the professional can scope the quote sensibly.
Tell us where you are and how far you are willing to look, since you searched for someone near you and travel matters for site visits.
questions: Are you on the Architects Registration Board register, and can you confirm that in writing?
Have you worked on interiors in buildings like mine, and can you talk me through how you approached a similar layout?
Will you handle building regulations approval and any planning permission, or is that down to me?
Will you bring in a structural engineer if walls need to come out, and how is that arranged?
What exactly is included in your appointment — drawings, specifications, lighting design, site visits — and what is charged separately?
How do you set your fees for a project like mine, and what would you need from me before quoting?

faqs.q: Do I need a registered architect for interior work?
faqs.a: Not always — architectural designers and technologists can do excellent interior work. But only people on the Architects Registration Board register can call themselves architects, so if that title matters to you, check the register before appointing anyone.

faqs.q: Will my project need building regulations approval?
faqs.a: Often, yes — particularly where walls are moved, structural work is involved or the use of the space changes. Your professional can help you navigate building regulations approval, which is a separate process from planning permission.

faqs.q: Can an interior architect help with lighting and finishes?
faqs.a: Yes. Lighting design transforms spaces, and finishes are part of how an interior is redesigned, so it is worth asking upfront what is included in the appointment and what is charged separately.
